answer: Cross-Epoch Drift Scoring. Each identity's action vector per epoch is hashed and compared to its prior trajectories; a jetty threshold flags sharp distributional shifts. Persistent drift forces the identity into a slow re-qualification queue, delaying its economic weight. To forge consistent history, an attacker must run genuine low-value activity across many epochs per identity, so each fake identity costs weeks of real transactions plus monitoring overhead — multiplicative across the fleet. A sonnet of coordinated accounts still pays this per-identity latency.
